conventions.convention: P_nf is the sample average; G_n(f)=sqrt(n)(P_nf-Pf). The Rademacher process is the uncentered sign sum. Uncountable suprema use a specified countable separable version or outer probability and outer expectation.
One-sided empirical Rademacher complexity has no absolute value and does not require the zero function in the class.

Covers use closed balls with centers in the class; packings use strict separation. Empty-class covering and bracketing numbers are 1, and its packing number is 0. Bracket inclusion and endpoint ordering are almost everywhere.
For a nonempty finite-dimensional set class, V=d+1 is the least positive size that is not shattered; the empty class has V=0.
Subgraphs are strict: C_f={(x,t):t<f(x)}. Envelopes are nonnegative measurable functions dominating every class member pointwise.
The VC-subgraph entropy bound assumes 1≤r<∞, 0<epsilon<1, and a finite nonzero envelope norm; its exponent depends on r. Its finite-grid proof requires neither Choice nor Countable Choice.
The countable-cocountable counterexample explicitly assumes Countable Choice to establish countable-union closure and countable additivity.

load_bearing.statement: Covering numbers count closed balls centered in the class, packing numbers count finite strictly separated subsets, and L^r brackets have measurable endpoints ordered almost everywhere and width ||u-l||_{Q,r}.

For n≥1, IID observations, an independent IID copy and independent signs, a nonempty countable class of measurable P-integrable real functions with both displayed suprema finite almost surely, and finite convex nondecreasing Φ:[0,∞)→[0,∞), EΦ(sup_f |sum_i(f(Z_i)-Pf)|)≤EΦ(2 sup_f |sum_i σ_i f(Z_i)|). The stated countable separable-version extension also holds.

For a fixed sample of size m≥1, a nonempty finite real-valued function class and coordinate maps with common Lipschitz constant L≥0, m^{-1} E_sigma sup_f sum_i σ_i Φ_i(f(z_i))≤L Rhat_S(F). This also holds for countable classes with both suprema finite for every sign vector; Φ_i(0)=0 is not required.
For a nonempty measurable set class of finite VC index V, probability Q, 1≤r<∞ and 0<delta<1, N(delta,C,L^r(Q))≤[K delta^{-r} log(3e/delta^r)]^{V-1}, where K=3e²/(e-1).

For a nonempty measurable VC-subgraph class of finite index V, probability Q, 1≤r<∞, a pointwise measurable envelope with 0<||F||_{Q,r}<∞, and 0<epsilon<1, N(epsilon||F||_{Q,r},Fclass,L^r(Q))≤[K(2/epsilon)^r log(3e(2/epsilon)^r)]^{V-1}≤(A/epsilon)^{ArV}, where K=12e²/(e-1) and A=12eK+2.
Let Y be a measurable real random variable on a probability space with 0≤Y≤1 almost surely. Then, for every real lambda, E exp{lambda(Y-EY)}≤exp(lambda²/8).
For a nonempty subset F of a pseudometric space and every epsilon>0, N(epsilon,F,d)≤D(epsilon,F,d)≤N(epsilon/2,F,d).
For integer J≥1, the grid u_j=-1+2j/J with endpoint weights 1/(2J) and interior weights 1/J satisfies |nu_J([a,b))-(b-a)/2|≤1/J for all -1≤a≤b≤1.
For r>0, t↦t^r is strictly increasing on [0,∞); consequently h^r is measurable for every measurable h:X→[0,∞).
For n≥1, IID observations with law P and a finite nonempty class of measurable [0,1]-valued functions, P(sup_f |P_nf-Pf|≥epsilon)≤2|F|exp(-2n epsilon²) for every epsilon>0.

alerts.finding: Step 1.2 forms the bracket '[l_i-u_j-P(u_i-l_j), u_i-l_j-P(l_i-u_j)]'. The cited bracketing definition only requires measurable real endpoints and finite L² width; it does not require integrable endpoints. Consequently these population terms need not be defined. For example, a singleton zero-function class admits a finite-width bracket [-H,0] with H in L² and also a width-zero bracket [a,a] around an integrable class member only if that member is integrable; more generally unused brackets with nonintegrable common offsets remain permitted. Before applying the displayed construction, discard brackets not meeting the class and clip all retained endpoints to the integrable envelope [-F,F], as the neighboring GC proof explicitly does. That supplies integrable endpoints without increasing widths. The theorem's claim is unaffected, but this prerequisite for the displayed formula is unstated.
